scope: All 26 existing Mollusca received an initial external-form correction and individual screenshot comparison. Models remain partly stylized and unmeasured. This is an authored educational reconstruction review, not independent specialist approval, a 90-percent accuracy score, validated biomechanics, physiology or a photorealism certification.
method: Synchronous main-viewer canvas captures: side/front/top Observe for every mollusc, an enabled action when implemented, plus selected octopus reach/support/underside phases. Actual reference photographs or shells are separate individuals, not fitted 3D coordinates or photographic model textures. Rejected preview, shadow-only and folded-scallop drafts are excluded from final totals.
sourceAccess: Selected authoritative descriptions, taxonomic context and primary indexed abstracts/results were consulted. No new measured trajectories were fitted. Octopus crawling draws only on Levy et al. 2015 abstract/process context, not its video or tracked coordinates; sucker context does not reconstruct full internal sucker anatomy. Nacella treatment text was read, not its Figure 8. Chlamys museum description was indexed text after direct access timed out. Existing historical citations retain their original access scope; inclusion does not assert a fresh full-text or figure review. No private paper figures are republished.
limits: Shells lack many internal diagnostic structures, natural epibionts and measured microtexture. Coiled-shell envelopes and sutures are external approximations, not reconstructed whorl volumes. Snail glides omit pedal/ciliary traction and mucus. Valve studies omit water, gills, particles and swimming forces. Octopus skin, arm ratios, papillae, sucker spacing and support/contact are qualitative; jetting, prey handling and physiology are absent. Near-unseen underside details cannot be verified from a dark capture. Existing species identities/photos are retained with their source caveats; this pass does not independently determine each specimen.
licensing: Original numerical geometry/surface code follows the project MIT license. No organism photograph or AI image was generated. Reference pixels retain the exact individual creators and grants below. Each comparison sheet includes a resized reference; reuse it under that photograph’s applicable license, including attribution/share-alike where required. Do not apply MIT to the photographs.
